subject: pe
title: Schema Theory
welcome_lead: Schmidt 1975 — generalised motor programmes adapted by parameters.
meta_desc: A-Level PE adventure on Schmidt's schema theory of motor learning.
final_note: Schemas explain why we can adapt skills to new situations we've never practised.

concepts.def: Schmidt 1975: generalised motor programmes adjusted by parameters.
Initial conditions + desired outcome → motor programme selection.
Initial conditions + sensory consequences → expected feedback.
Underlying pattern modifiable by parameters (force, timing).
Practising a skill in varied contexts; strengthens schemas.
Influence of one skill's learning on another's acquisition or performance.

walkthroughs.body_html: Schmidt argued varied practice builds richer schemas, enabling adaptation to novel situations.
Recall selects movement; recognition evaluates whether expected sensory feedback occurred.
Positive transfer aids new skills; negative transfer hinders (e.g., tennis grip into squash). Zero is no effect.

options: Skills are unique and not generalisable
